reasoning_notes: I gated candidates first on two hard signals: (1) chain purity - do all reported events belong to a single causal chain, or are they scattered across several unrelated chains (e.g. C-46 mixes chain1/2/3/4/5 events on one entity - classic artefact); and (2) causal-order compliance - does first_seen_day increase in the chain's stated order, or is a downstream event reported before its supposed cause (e.g. C-25 shows revenue_miss before yield_drop, C-56 shows account_churn before backlog_growth, C-0/C-44/C-1/C-13/C-37 show similar smaller reversals). Anything failing either check was pushed to the bottom regardless of report volume. Among order-compliant single-chain candidates, I then ranked by chain length (more consecutive causally-ordered links = stronger corroboration), by how many links rested on only 1 independent_sources (a lone report standing in for a whole link is the classic 'artefact of routine traffic' pattern), and by cumulative distinct_sites/distinct_regions (true cross-organisational spread vs. one or two loud sites). Top picks like C-9, C-29, C-58, C-39, C-42 combine 4-6 links in strict causal order, most/all links backed by 3+ independent sources, and coverage across 5-7 regions and 9-14 sites - hard to explain as coincidence or local noise. The 'real' cutoff (18 of 60) was drawn where chains still had >=3 links, correct order, and at most one weak (single-source) link, typically the terminal outcome event.
